analysis: The sampled-softmax trial completed successfully but failed to improve macro validation HR@10: 0.5613 versus the reported prior GRU baseline of 0.5737, a decrease of 0.0124. Electronics improved from 0.435 to 0.455; current HR@10 was 0.615 for Movies_and_TV, 0.590 for Industrial_and_Scientific, and 0.585 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Prior scores for those three categories were not supplied, so their individual changes cannot be quantified. Replacing independent positive/negative softplus terms with cross-entropy over one positive and eight uniform negatives did not improve the aggregate result in this run. Direct candidate competition was insufficient under the retained configuration; the available results do not establish why. These are validation findings only.
code_summary: One independently trained GRURec model per category, with exactly one selected checkpoint loaded for each dataset route. Architecture: 96-dimensional item embeddings, input LayerNorm, dropout 0.25, two GRU layers, linear projection and LayerNorm, normalized hidden states and tied normalized item embeddings, jointly learned item bias, and learned score scale capped at 30. Maximum history length defaults to 128. The sole experimental change was nine-class sampled-softmax cross-entropy at each valid sequence position, placing the positive at class zero alongside eight uniform negatives with target-collision resampling. Sampling, AdamW configuration, mixed precision, gradient clipping, history windows, seeds, deadlines, and validation HR@10 checkpoint selection with NDCG tie-breaking were retained. The predictor writer remained compatible with the unchanged architecture; no ensembles or checkpoint averaging were used.
